name: Halifax
title: Holidays in Halifax
intro: Lighthouses, lobster rolls and the world's highest tides on Canada's Atlantic coast. Here's what Halifax and Nova Scotia are like with the family.
facts_note: Check entry rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: June to October is best, with warm days, festivals and whale watching. Late September and October bring bright autumn colours. Winters are cold and snowy, and some sights close.

things.name: Halifax waterfront
things.blurb: A long boardwalk with ice cream, boats and a ferry across the harbour.

things.name: Maritime Museum of the Atlantic
things.blurb: Titanic objects and stories, as Halifax was where many victims were brought.

things.name: Halifax Citadel
things.blurb: A star-shaped fort with soldiers in kilts and a noon cannon.

things.name: Peggy's Cove
things.blurb: A famous lighthouse on granite rocks. Stay off the dark, wet rocks near the sea.

things.name: Bay of Fundy
things.blurb: The world's highest tides. Walk on the sea floor at low tide, then watch it fill.

things.name: Whale watching
things.blurb: Humpbacks and minke whales off the coast from June to October.

faqs.question: Is Halifax good for a family holiday?
faqs.answer: Yes, especially for a relaxed coastal road trip. It's friendly, easy-going and the closest bit of Canada to the UK.

faqs.question: How many nights do you need?
faqs.answer: Five to seven nights for Halifax and a loop round Nova Scotia's coast.

faqs.question: Do UK families need a visa?
faqs.answer: No, but British passport holders flying to Canada, children included, need an eTA, which you apply for online. Check GOV.UK for the current rules.

faqs.question: How long is the flight?
faqs.answer: About six hours from London, so it's one of the quickest ways to get to North America.
